page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance pairs these vCPUs with 32 GB of system memory, delivering a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It features hardware support for cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside standard AVX vector extensions, but lacks local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark assessments, the n2d-highmem-4 shows a distinct division between single-threaded execution and multi-core output. It achieves top 25% performance in stress-ng single-core tests and average scores in Geekbench single-core (1426) and PassMark encryption. However, total multi-core capacity registers in the bottom 25%, as reflected by a stress-ng multi-core score of 5386.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 6021.53. Uncached memory write bandwidth sits in the middle 50% at 28.03 GB/sec, while uncached read bandwidth drops to 38.56 GB/sec, indicating moderate memory throughput limitations under heavy concurrent access.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency standpoint, n2d-highmem-4 offers high memory capacity per core without requiring large vCPU counts. The instance is well suited for memory-intensive applications requiring low thread concurrency, such as small-to-medium in-memory caching, web application serving with large per-process memory footprints, and modest database processing. However, compute-heavy tasks like ray tracing, multi-threaded code compilation, or high-throughput batch data processing are constrained by its 2 physical cores and limited multi-threaded scaling.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 32 GB of system RAM, it maintains a generous 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI encryption extensions, though it lacks local storage drives and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests and average encryption processing, contrasted by weak multi-core scaling and uncached memory read bandwidth. With a PassMark memory score in the middle tier and 4.29 million Redis SET operations per second, this instance delivers adequate qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy, moderate-concurrency workloads. It is best suited for small in-memory caches, light database management, and RAM-bound background services.
